decisive_item.title: Nvidia GPU Debt Backstop Unleashes the AI Project Trinity: Capital, Offtake and Datacenters
decisive_item.who: Sharon AI (counterparty disclosure, reported by SemiAnalysis)
decisive_item.passage: Sharon disclosed a total backstop value of $4.88B

meaning.what: total value of NVIDIA's backstop on Sharon's 72MW Australian AI factory (up to 40,000 GB300)

kept_from_that_article.summary: SemiAnalysis said that, three years into the AI buildout, the general market's Nvidia shipment-volume and revenue estimates for the second half of 2026 remain materially below its own supply-chain tracking in its Accelerator Model, even as Nvidia revenue is rising sharply.
passages: Nvidia revenue is skyrocketing, and even 3 years into the build out, the general market is still materially lower on shipment volumes and revenue estimates for Nvidia in the 2nd half of this year versus our through supply chain tracking in the Accelerator Model .

kept_from_that_article.summary: SemiAnalysis forecast that AI debt financing will grow to more than $7 trillion outstanding by 2029, making it the second-largest asset-backed debt market after the roughly $13 trillion US mortgage-backed market, and that annual AI capex will exceed $2 trillion in 2028 with cumulative 2024–2029 AI capex of about $11.1 trillion, mainly funded by credit markets.
passages:
AI Debt Financing will become a multi-trillion-dollar credit market, with over $7T of debt outstanding by 2029 driven both by AI IT Capex and AI Datacenter Capex needs for Neoclouds, datacenter builders, and even hyperscalers. This will make it the second largest asset backed debt market after the US mortgage-backed financing market at just over $13T.
Annual AI Capex – including GPUs, networking, storage and attached CPU compute as well as for the Datacenters to house AI compute – will be well north of $2T in 2028. Cumulative AI Capex from 2024 to 2029 will reach ~$11.1T, and credit markets will be the main funding source for this buildout.

kept_from_that_article.summary: SemiAnalysis reported that Nvidia has begun backstopping GPU rental offtakes, providing Neoclouds a take-or-pay commitment and minimum revenue guarantee on underlying GPU capacity while taking a share of Neocloud revenue earned above the backstop level.
passages: This is why Nvidia has stepped in and has started backstopping GPU rental offtakes themselves . In the backstop program, Nvidia provides a take-or-pay commitment to Neoclouds – a minimum revenue guarantee on the underlying GPU capacity. In exchange for this backstop, Nvidia also shares in a portion of the Neocloud’s revenue earned above the backstop level.

kept_from_that_article.summary: SemiAnalysis said Nvidia has gone beyond GPU offtake backstops and has started backstopping datacenter leases as well, to help Neoclouds secure datacenter capacity.
passages: Datacenter: However, even with the backstop in place, securing the final leg of the Trinity and obtaining datacenter capacity remains challenging absent a creative datacenter rental structure or resorting to a self-built datacenter. Here, Nvidia is diving even deeper, as it has started backstopping datacenter leases.

kept_from_that_article.summary: SemiAnalysis described Nvidia's backstop program as typically six years, with Nvidia standing ready to buy compute at pre-agreed price levels that vary over time and each Neocloud negotiating individual revenue-share and backstop schedules; it presented an illustrative lower-end backstop pricing curve averaging $2.36 per GPU-hour over six years and said it expects most Neoclouds to negotiate higher backstops.
passages: Nvidia’s backstop program is typically six years in length, and during these six years, Nvidia stands ready to purchase compute at pre-agreed price levels that vary over the time period. Each Neocloud is expected to negotiate the backstop terms individually, and we can expect that different Neoclouds may end up with different revenue share and backstop schedules. The below table is an illustrative example to explain the basic terms of the program – we present a backstop pricing curve that we believe to be on the lower end of the backstop range – in this case at an average of $2.36 over the six-year period, but we expect that most Neoclouds will negotiate higher backstops.

kept_from_that_article.summary: SharonAI announced in June 2026 a 72MW AI factory in Australia under a six-year Nvidia backstop, scaling to as many as 40,000 GB300s, with SharonAI disclosing a total backstop value of $4.88 billion, or an implied floor of about $2.33/hour/GPU on average over six years; SharonAI said its footprint would grow to 132MW with 102MW contracted and guided to more than 55,000 Nvidia GPUs in total, including the 40,000 backstopped GB300s, by mid-2027.
passages: The first is SharonAI’s 72MW AI factory in Australia. Announced in June 2026, the deal has SharonAI scaling up to as many as 40,000 GB300s under a six-year backstop. Sharon disclosed a total backstop value of $4.88B, which works out to an implied floor of about $2.33/hr/GPU on average over the six year period. Sharon AI’s footprint is now set to grow to 132MW with 102MW contracted, and the company guides to reaching more than 55,000 Nvidia GPUs in total (inclusive of the 40,000 GB300s backstopped) by mid-2027.

kept_from_that_article.summary: Firmus announced on June 29, 2026 a 360MW AI cluster in Batam, Indonesia under an Nvidia backstop, likely to be housed in a DayOne facility in Kabil Industrial Tech Park; Firmus expects $25 billion to $30 billion of customer revenue over the six years, and SemiAnalysis expects a portion of revenue above the backstop to be shared with Nvidia.
passages: Firmus’s 360MW AI Cluster in Batam, Indonesia is the next major project announced with an Nvidia backstop. It will likely be housed in a DayOne facility in Kabil Industrial Tech Park (KITP). Announced just recently on June 29 th , 2026, this project shows the scale at which Nvidia is rolling out the backstop program.

The Nvidia backstop allows Firmus to grow their business by an order of magnitude. As per Nvidia’s key objectives that we outlined above, the focus of this cluster will be to open up compute to a variety of AI Natives, Enterprises and Inference Providers, with many different rental tenors to be offered. Firmus announced that they expect $25B to $30B of customer revenue over the six years. We expect a portion of the revenue above the backstop level will be shared with Nvidia as per the structure we outlined earlier today.

kept_from_that_article.summary: The Information reported that NVIDIA is providing financial guarantees to young GPU cloud service providers that lease or rent its GPUs: if those companies fail to secure enough AI developers to rent the capacity, NVIDIA will repurchase their unsold GPU capacity at a pre-agreed price, and in return NVIDIA receives a percentage of the cloud providers' revenue that declines over the contract term. GPU cloud providers Firmus and Sharon AI have joined the program, and three executives with existing ties to NVIDIA confirmed the arrangement, per The Information.
passages: On July 1, according to the technology news outlet The Information, NVIDIA is providing financial guarantees to young cloud service providers that lease or rent its GPUs—if these companies fail to secure enough AI developers to rent their computing capacity, NVIDIA will repurchase their unsold GPU capacity at a pre-agreed price.

In return, NVIDIA will receive a percentage of these cloud providers’ revenue, with the revenue-sharing rate gradually declining over the term of the contract. GPU cloud providers Firmus and Sharon AI have already joined the program, and three executives with existing business ties to NVIDIA confirmed the arrangement.

kept_from_that_article.summary: On July 1, NVIDIA published a statement on its official website announcing a new business model combining revenue sharing with credit support, enabling AI cloud providers to procure NVIDIA infrastructure without bearing the full upfront capital expenditure, and to offer computing services to downstream AI-native enterprises, model developers and corporate clients. Per NVIDIA's official press release, the company will earn not only standard product revenue but also an additional share of cloud service revenue, creating a usage-based, recurring revenue stream.
passages: On July 1, NVIDIA published a statement on its official website announcing a new business model that combines revenue sharing with credit support, enabling AI cloud providers to procure NVIDIA infrastructure without bearing the full upfront capital expenditure, and allowing them to offer computing services to downstream AI-native enterprises, model developers, and corporate clients.

According to NVIDIA’s official press release, the company will earn not only standard product revenue but also an additional share of cloud service revenue, creating a usage-based, recurring revenue stream.

kept_from_that_article.summary: Sharon AI and Firmus are the first cloud providers participating in NVIDIA's new revenue-sharing/credit-support model. Sharon AI plans to deploy up to 40,000 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GB300 GPUs, while Firmus is constructing a DSX AI Factory campus in Batam, Indonesia, expected to scale up to 360 megawatts and accommodate up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs.

passages: Nvidia 's next marquee product — the Kyber rack-scale architecture designed to house its 2027 Rubin Ultra chips — has been delayed by more than 12 months to 2028, according to research firm SemiAnalysis, the latest in a string of reported setbacks raising questions about the AI giant's product roadmap.

The design mounts graphics processing units in compute trays that sit vertically instead of horizontally to boost density and reduce latency, and had been slated to debut with Vera Rubin Ultra, Nvidia's next-generation rack-scale system, in 2027 .
